name: revenue unit
note: The value in Australian dollars of the Northern Territory's revenue unit for each financial year from 2018-19 to 2026-27, from the notices the Commissioner of Territory Revenue gives under section 6(1) of the Revenue Units Act 2009 in the Northern Territory Government Gazette, each read 2026-10-30 from the copy the Northern Territory Library holds on Territory Stories (its legal-deposit archive of the Gazette), and from the Act's reprints on legislation.nt.gov.au. Section 5 of the Act says a new value 'takes effect on 1 July of the new financial year', and each notice names that day, so every value here is from 1 July and holds to 30 June of the next year. Reading for 2020-21: the Gazette of 26 February 2020 (G8) notified $1.24 from 1 July 2020, but the Treasury and Finance Legislation Amendment Act 2020 (Act No. 28 of 2020, assented 15 December 2020), whose Part 3 'is taken to have commenced on 1 July 2020', made section 4(1)(a) read 'is $1.21 until 30 June 2021'; the reprint as in force at 1 July 2020 shows it. So the law held the unit at $1.21 through 2020-21, and no step is written for 1 July 2020: the 2019 value ($1.21) holds until the 2021 notice ($1.24 from 1 July 2021). The reprint as in force at 1 July 2022 fixes $1.27 'for the financial year ending on 30 June 2023', which the Gazette of 30 June 2022 (S36) notified. Not held: years before 2018-19. Territory Stories' search found a notice in G7 of 13 February 2013 and the one for 1 July 2015 ($1.15, G6 of 11 February 2015), but none for 1 July 2014, 2016 or 2017, and a run with a missing year would make a value hold too long, so the series starts at 2018-19. NT Treasury's own pages (treasury.nt.gov.au, 'New value of a revenue unit from 1 July 2025' and its revenue units page) and nt.gov.au, where the Gazette is published, answered this client with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment' check on 2026-10-30 and were not read. The 2027-28 value is not published on 2026-10-30. The form doesn't hold the Act's rule that a fee worked from revenue units is rounded down to the nearest $1 (section 3(2)), nor its indexation formula (section 4). A fee or charge worked from revenue units is rounded down to the nearest $1 where it isn't a multiple of $1 (s 3(2)): held as the unit's roundDown, 1 (the lead, 2026-10-30).

sources.title: Revenue Units Act 2009 (NT), as in force at 1 July 2022 (current reprint, legislation.nt.gov.au)
sources.said: As in force at 1 July 2022 ... (a) $1.27 for the financial year ending on 30 June 2023; and ... If the monetary value of a revenue unit calculated under section 4 for a financial year (the new financial year) increases from that of the previous financial year, the new value: (a) takes effect on 1 July of the new financial year; and ... The Commissioner of Territory Revenue must notify the new value of a revenue unit by Gazette notice before the date on which the new value takes effect. ... However, if the amount obtained for the fee or charge is not a multiple of $1, the amount is to be rounded down to the nearest $1.
